claims.text: The coating system is equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn.
Increasing grain-boundary density by producing a nanocrystalline microstructure improves the wear resistance of equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn coatings.
Higher grain-boundary density promotes grain-boundary sliding in the coating.
Higher grain-boundary density promotes dynamic recrystallization during wear.
Delayed crack initiation reduces abrasive wear.
Standard processing produces a coarse-grained equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn coating.
Rapid-solidification processing can produce nanocrystalline and coarse-grained coatings of otherwise identical composition.
Grain-boundary density governs the availability of grain boundaries for plastic-deformation mechanisms.
The nanocrystalline coating accommodates deformation more effectively than the coarse-grained coating.
Under identical wear conditions, the nanocrystalline coating will have a lower wear rate than the coarse-grained baseline.
Under identical wear conditions, the nanocrystalline coating will have less severe wear scars than the coarse-grained baseline.
Increasing grain size will increase wear rate by reducing the grain boundaries available for plastic deformation.
The proposed grain-size effect should hold at room temperature in air under constant-load, constant-speed reciprocating wear conditions when grain-boundary-mediated deformation dominates.
Rapid solidification may introduce texture or defect-density changes that also affect wear resistance.
